statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is elevated after the Nasdaq opened higher and reached a fresh intraday record, while the active Fed-speaker window keeps Stress extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES; current Tail is elevated during the cash-open continuation and 14:05–14:20 UTC Fed-speaker cluster.
headline: Nasdaq record-high continuation lifts Tail into the Fed-speaker window
body: Reuters reported the Nasdaq opened higher and reached a fresh intraday record with positive breadth as technology regained leadership. Falling oil and Treasury yields are supportive cross-asset amplifiers, but granular NQ pullback evidence is not fresh enough to confirm a persistent no-retracement path.

lookbackSummary: Monday’s trend-up phase briefly pushed Tail into the high band before normalization. Tuesday’s overnight and European-session readings stayed mostly low, while the 13:00 UTC assessment remained low-Tail but extreme-Stress immediately before the U.S. cash open.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is elevated because the cash open has continued to a fresh Nasdaq record while supportive cross-assets are aligned. The risk should de-escalate if meaningful retracements develop after the Fed-speaker cluster; persistent extension near session highs would keep the danger window elevated.

forecast.analysis: The Nasdaq has already opened higher and printed a fresh intraday record, while oil and yields eased. Tail is elevated for this hour because the open has extended upward, but the lack of verified shallow-pullback evidence keeps it below high.
drivers: Fresh Nasdaq intraday record after the cash open
Oil and Treasury yields are easing

news.title: Nasdaq hits intraday record high as tech stocks regain footing
Wall St futures pause after AI rally, focus on Mideast tensions

forecast.analysis: After the Fed-speaker cluster, Tail remains elevated only if the record-high move keeps extending with weak retracements. A meaningful pullback or rotation away from the high would reduce the path risk.
drivers: Retracement depth after the record-high print

forecast.analysis: By the U.S. midday transition, WATCH is appropriate only if the opening move remains directionally efficient. Broader two-way rotation would favor a mixed regime and lower Tail.
Barkin’s 17:00 UTC remarks add event stress. Tail stays in WATCH unless the market enters the speech already stretched near an extreme and extends further without meaningful mean reversion.
After Barkin, Tail should ease if price discovery is orderly and counter-moves deepen. A delayed second leg with little retracement would keep WATCH conditions in place.
Late-session Tail is most sensitive to whether the Nasdaq would hold near a session extreme. Persistent extension into power hour would keep WATCH; rotation away from extremes would lower risk.
The cash-close hour carries modest WATCH risk if directional pressure survives into the closing auction. A balanced close would favor normalization despite the high-stress day.
CME maintenance reduces continuous price discovery. Tail is low unless a strong unresolved cash-session move carries into the break and leaves a clear gap risk for the reopen.
At the Globex reopen, Tail stays low unless the prior cash-session move gaps further in the same direction. Stable reopening trade would support normalization.
drivers: Reopen gap versus the cash close

forecast.analysis: Early Globex conditions should be quieter absent a fresh geopolitical or policy catalyst. Tail remains low unless liquidity thins around a renewed directional shock.
The late U.S. evening is expected to be lower-stress. Tail remains low unless a new cross-asset shock creates a one-way futures move before Asia becomes active.
Around the Asia transition, Tail remains low under orderly trade. A large gap with aligned regional technology moves would be the main reason for reassessment.
Asian liquidity can widen moves, but Tail remains low without repeated extension or failed pullbacks. Directional regional equity confirmation would raise conditional risk modestly.
Mid-Asia trade is expected to normalize if no new catalyst arrives. Tail remains low unless futures hold at an overnight extreme with little two-way trade.
drivers: Absence or presence of two-way trade

forecast.analysis: Later Asian trade carries limited standalone Tail risk. A fresh geopolitical development or synchronized semiconductor move would be the principal escalation route.
Ahead of Europe, Tail remains low if the overnight range is respected. A clean breakout with shallow retracements would move the regime away from normal.
The European handoff can increase cross-asset interaction. Tail stays low unless yields, oil and technology equities align with a directional NQ breakout.
As European liquidity deepens, WATCH becomes plausible if a directional overnight break persists. Mean-reverting rotation would keep the regime mixed rather than trend-driven.
The European morning remains a conditional WATCH zone if the overnight direction survives repeated tests. Failed continuation would quickly reduce Tail.
drivers: Repeated tests of the overnight direction

forecast.analysis: Late European trade should remain low-Tail unless a new macro or geopolitical catalyst produces aligned cross-asset continuation before U.S. premarket liquidity builds.
U.S. premarket participation begins to matter more. WATCH is appropriate if the overnight move is still intact and semiconductors or megacaps reinforce the same direction.
Approaching the U.S. data window, Stress rises. Tail stays WATCH unless premarket price action becomes one-way and holds near an extreme into the next cash open.
The hour before the next cash open carries higher event sensitivity. Tail remains WATCH unless premarket extension is already persistent with weak retracements.

The next U.S. cash-open hour includes the 13:30 UTC open and 13:45 UTC flash PMI. Tail is conditionally elevated only if the release/open combination produces persistent extension and failed retracements.
drivers: 13:45 UTC S&P Global Flash US PMI

forecastDetail.comment: Record-high cash-open continuation raises conditional Tail, but no verified shallow-pullback sequence is available yet.
Elevated Tail persists only if the post-speaker move remains one-way; meaningful retracement would de-escalate it.
Midday WATCH depends on whether the opening trend remains efficient rather than rotating two-way.
Barkin adds event stress; Tail stays WATCH unless an already stretched path extends through the remarks.
Post-Barkin risk centers on a delayed second leg versus orderly retracement.
Power-hour WATCH depends on session-extreme holding and weak counter-moves.
